source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 1 (ISLB A1) · lesson 11. Exercises reused from the lesson.

title.en: The Adhan: the call to prayer

topic: Allah's daily invitation to prayer, and what its words mean

learn.en: The Adhan is a gentle reminder, five times a day, that it is time to pray.
learn.title: Allah's invitation

learn.en: The person who calls the Adhan in the mosque is called the mu'adhdhin. The first was Bilal.
learn.title: The mu'adhdhin

learn.en: The words of the Adhan were shown in a dream to Abdullah ibn Zayd, and the Prophet ﷺ asked Bilal to call them.
learn.title: How it began

learn.en: When you hear the Adhan — from a mosque, a clock or an app — pause your game or homework and get ready to pray.
learn.title: When you hear it

learn.en: The Adhan says “come to prayer” and “come to success”: true success comes from remembering Allah.
learn.title: Prayer is success

words.en: the one who calls the adhan
Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest

words.ar: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ
words.en: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah
I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest
There is no god but Allah

order.en: Put the words of the Adhan in order

quiz.en: How many times a day is the Adhan called?
What is the person who calls the Adhan called?
What should you do when you hear the Adhan?
opts: Pause and get ready for prayer

quiz.en: True or false? “Hayya ‘ala l-falah” means “come to success”.

think.q: Why do you think the Adhan puts “come to prayer” and “come to success” next to each other?
think.a: Because real success isn't finishing a game level — it's remembering Allah and praying.

parents.summary: The Adhan: the call to prayer five times a day, the mu'adhdhin (Bilal was the first), and the meaning of its words.
parents.tip: When you hear the adhan at home, pause together and repeat its words softly.
